<a id="p175-a1-p175-a2--delegates-directed-through-spa-toward-berlin"></a>

## Delegates directed through Spa toward Berlin

**Sources on this page:** p175 A1, p175 A2.

<a id="edition-cases-people-spa-berlin-delegates-delegates-directed-through-spa-toward-berlin"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

**Prior body and historical discussion:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel,
Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern
Front of World War I* (2016), §6.4, author PDF page 24,
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461). That discussion
explicitly cites p175 A together with p172 C. This edition adds a
source-exact transcript and quantified repairs; it does not claim the
travel message as a new historical decipherment.

Childs printed p175 A, PDF page 178, contains two parts under
`ZM v SY (10.57 p.m., November 10th); VE (10) 2 TLE`.
The text directs delegates by train or car to Spa, with onward travel
toward Berlin on the following date-like field. Its time remains
partly unknown. The two parts have native lengths **192** and **104**
coordinates and use the unchanged published **Nov10–12** key.


<a id="source-p175-a1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-spa-berlin-delegates-p175-a1"></a>

### p175 A1

The [source crop](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p175_A1.png)
directly decrypts to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HPTMXMANNITAED1XNAMUTXZUGLEICHFUERHPTMXVXWEIHERXEXIX2XXABGEORDNETEMITZUGODETAUTOSONACHSPALEITENX
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate repairs give this readable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
HPTMXMANNSTAEDTXNAMURXZUGLEICHFUERHPTMXVXWEIHERXEXIX2XXABGEORDNETEMITZUGODERAUTOSONACHSPALEITENX
```

</details>

It addresses the officer named by the candidate `MANNSTAEDT` at Namur,
also for Captain von Weiher, and directs delegates by train or car to
Spa. The exact address field `EXIX2` is retained. This edition does not
independently identify either officer, expand the unit field or identify
the delegates as particular historical people.

The separate [Namur order witnesses](171.md#edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses) have
`HPTMANNSTAEDT` without this part's separator after `HPTM`. That string
can instead be segmented as a title followed by `STAEDT`. Their related
wording supports comparison, but does not establish a shared person
or make these messages exact retransmissions. The earlier source
reconciliation remains unchanged.

<a id="source-p175-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-spa-berlin-delegates-p175-a2"></a>

### p175 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p175_A2.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DASSWEITERFAHRTNACHBERLINAM11X11X?X03XNACWMXOHLRM4BX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate repair changes `NACWM` to `NACHM`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DASSWEITERFAHRTNACHBERLINAM11X11X?X03XNACHMXOHLRM4BX
```

</details>

The continuation gives onward travel to Berlin on `11X11` at
`?X03 NACHM`, followed by `OHLRM4B`. All these labels remain literal.
The unknown time digit has domain **56789** under the published partial
square. It is not a missing coordinate. Enumerating all **120** full
square completions gives five compatible literal time digits, each in
24 completions, with the exact same candidate ciphertext.

The earlier paper describes a Berlin arrival at 15:00. That historical
narrative is credited separately; the present source edition does not
borrow its time or change `03`, and the wording here concerns onward
travel rather than an independently verified arrival.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> … dass Weiterfahrt nach Berlin am 11.11., 5.03 nachm. OHL RM4B.

<details>

```text

```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-people-spa-berlin-delegates-exact-cost-and-evidence"></a>

### Exact cost and evidence

The two parts contain **296 observed coordinates**, **148 plaintext
positions**, **147 fixed raw labels**, and the same 147 fixed labels
after repairs. They require **five observed-coordinate substitutions**,
with no fill, gap, deletion or key change. The unknown time remains
unknown; no increase in the fixed-label count is claimed for this pair.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting"></a>

## p175 B2 — Payments through October and cheque arrival acknowledgments

**Edition context:** Payments through October and cheque acknowledgements.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting-payments-through-october-and-cheque-acknowledgements"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs printed p175 B, PDF page 178, supplies a source-labeled **second
part**, received at **18:02 on 10 November**. Its 204 printed slots
include ten dashes. The native frame reads with the unchanged published
**Nov7–9** key. The receipt date is preserved; it is not used to substitute
the neighboring messages' Nov10–12 key.

The fragment concerns marks paid through the end of October, arrival
notices for cheques and `HAUPTWECHSELAMT`. Its missing first part is not
reconstructed, and no completed payment amount or transaction outcome
is inferred.

<a id="source-p175-b2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting-p175-b2"></a>

### p175 B2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 204-coordinate frame:**

```text
VO??8XBISENDUOCTOTE?GEZAHLT?N?ARKXFERNERANKUNFTSANZE?GEUEBERAM?XGESANDTE?HEKSXHAUPTWECHS?GA?T89240?11?
```

**Edited output — same native frame:** Four observed-coordinate
substitutions and eight printed-dash fills give:

```text
VOM?8XBISENDEOCTOBERGEZAHLTENMARKXFERNERANKUNFTSANZEIGEUEBERAM?XGESANDTECHEKSXHAUPTWECHSELAMT89240?11?
```

</details>

**Readable German — word spacing and punctuation of that candidate:**

> Vom ?8 bis Ende October gezahlten Mark. Ferner Ankunftsanzeige über
> am ? gesandte Cheks. Hauptwechselamt 89240?11?

The first sentence is a surviving clause fragment, not a reconstruction
of the missing first part. The spellings `OCTOBER` and `CHEKS` remain
visible. `VOM?8`, `AM?` and the final code are retained without normalizing
dates, amounts or reference numbers.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **am 6. gesandte Cheks** and the literal closing **892409116**, without additional coordinate changes or fills. The opposite assignment gives am 5. and 892409115. The final label is preserved as transmitted, rather than normalized to a date or matched to another reception’s separator.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting-what-the-question-marks-mean-here"></a>

### Unresolved positions and their domains

The four unknown positions have different origins:

| Literal field | Plaintext position | Full domain | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `VOM?8` | 3 | `1GIKNY` | One unfilled printed coordinate; the value is not restricted to digits |
| `AM?` | 62 | `56` | Both coordinates are observed; square cell `VF` is unassigned |
| `89240?11?`, first question mark | 98 | `5679JMZ` | One unfilled printed coordinate |
| `89240?11?`, final question mark | 101 | `56` | The same unassigned `VF` cell as position 62 |

Positions 62 and 101 must agree under an unchanged key. The source
does not select 5 or 6. The separate historical military constraint
proposed elsewhere for this key is not applied here.

All **72** combinations of the two possible full-square completions and
the two remaining printed-coordinate fills are retained as complete
compatibility witnesses. They re-encrypt exactly with the stated edited
coordinates. This enumeration verifies the remaining ambiguity; it
does not supply a historical completion.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-hauptwechselamt-accounting-exact-source-scope"></a>

### Exact source scope

The [source crop](../../experiments/hauptwechselamt_accounting/sources/p175_B.png)
has **204 printed slots**, **194 observed coordinates**, and **102
plaintext positions**. The raw reading fixes 90 labels; the edited
candidate fixes 98. There are **four observed-coordinate substitutions**
and **eight printed-dash fills**, with two printed dashes still unfilled.
No length change, source deletion or key change is made.

The earlier OCR-derived stream was shorter and produced an unreadable
candidate. The present contribution is source retranscription and
explicit arithmetic under the published key, without a historical
first-decipherment claim. Lasry and colleagues retain credit for the
period key; the paper's separate p175 A travel discussion is not claimed
as a prior reading of this financial fragment.

[Inputs](../../experiments/hauptwechselamt_accounting/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/hauptwechselamt_accounting/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/hauptwechselamt_accounting/README.md)
provide the literal source, every coordinate repair and all remaining
position domains.

**Later copy evidence:** The independently received p172 D2 supplies the two
remaining printed-dash values for `VOM18` and `89240911?` under the explicit
matching-second-part hypothesis. The conservative candidate keeps the four
original observed-coordinate substitutions and fixes 100/102 labels with
ten source-mask fills; its final `?` still shares cell VF with the date-like
field after AM. A separate common-copy ending X costs one additional
observed change. The [complete reconciliation](../../experiments/accounting_copy_reconciliation/README.md)
preserves both original editions, all five source disagreements, the two
unsupported ordinary-word repairs, and both global square completions.

## Romanian ultimatum and the crossing near Rustschuk

**Sources on this page:** p175 C1, p175 C2.

**Related source pages:** [p176 A5](176.md#source-p176-a5).

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-romanian-ultimatum-and-the-crossing-near-rustschuk"></a>



**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three newly source-edited parts belong to Childs's six-part message
on printed pp175–176, PDF pages 178–179. The repeated header is
`LP v NKJ (5.40 p.m., November 10th); VON UKS KR 0915 (10/11) 6 TLE`.
Its fourth part is the existing [p176a challenge](176.md#edition-cases-p176a), whose
breakthrough proposal retains prior credit to **Norbert and Max Baertl
in 2017**. This frozen three-record companion edition left two other
surviving parts unread; separate later editions now address C3 and A6.
Those parts remain excluded from its original three-record count.

The message reports that the Romanian government has presented an
ultimatum to evacuate its territory or lay down weapons. It then reports
French troops beginning to cross the Danube near Rustschuk and fighting
in progress. A later part discusses sending messages and material first
to Hermannstadt. These are statements in the intercepted report, not
independent confirmation of the events or their timing.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-p175-c1"></a>

### p175 C1

The [first-part source](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C1.png)
has 212 printed slots, including three dashes. Its direct reading is:

**Raw output:**


</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions and three printed-dash fills give:

</details>

The body says that the Romanian government has just issued an ultimatum
to clear the territory within the repeated literal `24X24` hours. The
prefix `JUDORTX1XAX11212OM` remains unidentified and unchanged. The
two copies of `24` are not summed or replaced by another duration.

It completes the ultimatum with the alternative of laying down weapons,

unchanged. Their value remains in **56789**. All 120 injective square
completions preserve the candidate ciphertext and give five equal-digit
possibilities, each in 24 completions. No historical hour is chosen.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-surviving-unread-parts-and-the-earlier-challenge"></a>

### Surviving unread parts and the earlier challenge

The source sequence is C1, C2, C3 on p175, followed by A4, A5, A6 on
p176. C3 has **217** printed slots against a stated length of **222**;
the missing five coordinates have no selected location. A6 has **160**
printed slots, of which **86** are dashes. Both are retained as source
context within this frozen companion edition, with no contribution to its
three-record totals. The later [conditional C3 withdrawal edition](#edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup)
now supplies a readable candidate while preserving all tied loss layouts.
The separate [conditional A6 coal-train fragment](176.md#edition-cases-military-p176-coal-train-fragment) now proposes 48/80 positions through 44 printed-mask fills and no observed-coordinate changes; its routing field and later tail remain raw.

A4 is already cataloged as p176a. Its earlier reconstructed text and
missing-block assumptions remain separate from these native-frame
companions. Being part of the same source-labeled message does not
independently prove the earlier reconstructed letters.

<a id="edition-cases-military-romanian-ultimatum-companions-exact-scope-of-the-edition"></a>

### Exact scope of the edition

The three new records contain **588 printed slots**, **580 observed
coordinates**, and **294 plaintext positions**. Their raw readings fix
**284** positions; the separately recorded candidates fix **291** after
**six known-coordinate substitutions and seven printed-dash fills**.
One printed dash and two occurrences of an unknown key label remain.
There is no modeled gap, deletion or key change in those three records.

Earlier unreviewed screening already contained the readable C2 and A5
bodies; C1 was garbled in a shorter OCR-derived frame. The present
contribution is exact source transcription, the full arithmetic and
uncertainty record, and a transparent assembly with prior credit.
No first historical decipherment claim is made.

The [package](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/README.md),
[inputs](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/certificates.json)
preserve all coordinates, domains, repairs, source crops, unread context,
and complete compatibility witnesses for the unresolved fields.

## p175 C3 — Conditional withdrawal report via Kronstadt and Hermannstadt

**Edition context:** Withdrawal from the Danube and Sereth front: p175 C3.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup-withdrawal-from-the-danube-and-sereth-front-p175-c3"></a>



**Source analysis and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This source-defined third part becomes readable under an explicit
five-coordinate loss model. It reports a withdrawal toward the mountains
from the Danube and Sereth front, with a route via Kronstadt and
Hermannstadt. **The plaintext and source alignment remain conditional**:
six placements of one contiguous missing block fit the edited candidate
at the same observed-coordinate cost, and a broader loss family has
six lower-cost alignments.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup-the-source-and-its-length"></a>

### The source and its length

Childs printed p175 C3, PDF page 178, belongs to the six-part message under
`LP v NKJ (5.40 p.m., November 10th); VON UKS KR 0915 (10/11) 6 TLE`.
The [literal part](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C3.png)
contains **217** printed slots, including four dashes. The enlarged
[header](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C3_heading_detail.png)
reads **RICHI-222**. The length difference is therefore **five**, but
the page does not mark where those missing coordinates belong.

The older source package keeps this part as frozen unread context.
This follow-up adds one newly cataloged reading of the same physical
record; the other five source parts and the existing p176a challenge
are not counted again.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup-raw-and-edited-output"></a>

### Raw and edited output

For display, insert one five-coordinate erased block before source
coordinate **95**. This is the smallest of six equally cheap placements
for the candidate, chosen as a stable representative. All indices are
zero-based. The published **Nov10–12** square and ranks are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional frame with five missing coordinates:**

```text
OK?XG?HTHE?TENACHT?ONDONAU?UND?ERETHFR?NTAUFGE?IRGQQURUECKXWIRDUEBERXKRONSTADTXHERMANNSTADTXRIWHTUNGXKLUZ?NBUR0
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame:** Four observed-coordinate
substitutions, four printed-dash fills and five unprinted-coordinate
fills give the following **111-position candidate**:

```text
OKMXGEHTHEUTENACHTVONDONAUXUNDSERETHFRONTAUFGEBIRGEZURUECKXWIRDUEBERXKRONSTADTXHERMANNSTADTXRICHTUNGXKLUZENBURG
```

</details>

**Readable German — punctuation and word spacing of the conditional candidate; the final ellipsis marks continuation into the next part:**

> O.K.M. geht heute Nacht von Donau- und Serethfront auf Gebirge zurück.
> Wird über Kronstadt, Hermannstadt Richtung Kluzenburg …

The second sentence continues into the next source part. That part is
the separately attributed [p176a challenge](176.md#edition-cases-p176a), whose earlier
breakthrough proposal has its own missing-block and editorial assumptions.
Its wording is not imported as independent proof of this reconstruction.

The source-derived spelling **KLUZENBURG** remains visible. The raw final
`0` is repaired through one specific observed-coordinate change; this
does not assign a new value to the key's `0` label. The interpretation
of `OKM` and the report's actual historical fulfillment are not separately
established by this source edition.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup-why-there-is-no-unique-recovered-gap"></a>

### Tied gap locations under the stated model

Every possible position for one contiguous five-coordinate loss was
checked: **218** source positions. Two frozen language models both rank
position **96** first, while several neighboring positions also produce
coherent partial readings. Ranking supplied a useful interval for
inspection, not a proof of a unique historical location.

For the complete candidate, the exact minimum over this family is four
observed-coordinate substitutions at each of these six gap starts:

```text
95, 96, 98, 99, 100, 101
```

If a whole five-letter group is assumed to have disappeared between
surviving printed groups, **95 and 100** remain tied. The source provides
no fixed omission marker to choose between them.

Allowing the five missing coordinates to be distributed arbitrarily
reduces the candidate's minimum to **three substitutions**. An exact
dynamic program over all missing-position sets finds **six** optimal
alignments, all with a local 1 + 3 + 1 loss pattern. Those six are also
fully retained. This broader result changes the loss assumption; it
does not prove that three separate losses actually occurred.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p175-c3-withdrawal-followup-repair-costs-and-evidence"></a>

### Repair costs and evidence

The displayed placement at 95 changes source coordinates
**97 G→X, 172 D→A, 174 F→D, and 209 V→F**. It fills printed dashes
**57→D, 58→D, 59→F, and 119→V**, and inserts `VVGXX`.
The resulting candidate re-encrypts exactly. Every tied alternative
has its own source mapping and equally explicit certificate.

This one record has **217 printed slots**, **213 observed coordinates**,
a **222-coordinate conditional frame**, and **111 plaintext positions**.
The displayed raw frame fixes **102** labels; the edited candidate fixes
111. Across all 218 unselected one-block frames, the common singleton
reading fixes **zero** positions. Thus the readable raw text itself
depends on choosing a frame; the complete candidate is a further
editorial layer.

Twelve newly composed synthetic controls test the screening procedure.
Both models' predeclared primary objective places a truth-compatible
layout first in all twelve. Secondary objectives fail on some controls,
and the controls have no added observed-coordinate errors. They support
this bounded method, without providing a historical confidence percentage.
The models are also correlated through their shared book component.

The [full analysis](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/README.md),
[screen results](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/screen_results.json),
and [certificate](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/certificates.json)
preserve all layouts, controls, rankings, exact minima and source indices.
No key cell is changed, no first historical decipherment claim is made,
and no exact cross-copy was accepted from the bounded corpus search.
